meta.honesty: Curated + graded. Vendor logical-qubit claims are frequently DEMONSTRATION or POSTSELECTED results, not production systems - each is labeled. CRQC (cryptographically-relevant quantum computer) timelines are ESTIMATES with wide error bars; this page does not assert a break date. The 'live feed' is machine-collected and UNVERIFIED - kept strictly separate from this curated base.

hardware.intro: Six qubit modalities compete on different axes (fidelity, connectivity, coherence, gate speed, scalability). No modality has won; the practical winner will likely be whoever reaches hundreds of fault-tolerant LOGICAL qubits first. Physical-qubit counts are marketing until paired with fidelity and error correction.

modalities.name: Superconducting transmon
modalities.principle: Microwave-driven Josephson-junction circuits at ~15 mK; fast (~microsecond) gates, chip-fab-friendly, but short coherence (~100 us) and mostly nearest-neighbor connectivity.
modalities.strengths: Fast gates; mature fabrication; largest physical-qubit counts.
modalities.weaknesses: Short coherence; limited connectivity; cryogenic overhead; wiring fan-out.

best_known.value: distance-7, 101 qubits, 0.143%/cycle; Lambda=2.14 per +2 distance; 2.4x over best physical qubit
materially improved; roadmap to Kookaburra ~4,158 physical qubits + qLDPC memory (~360 qubits, 7,500 gates)

modalities.roadmap: IBM: modular Quantum System Two -> 100,000+ qubits via chip-to-chip links; 200 logical qubits by 2029 (target). Google: fault-tolerant logical qubits before 2030 (target).

modalities.name: Trapped ion
modalities.principle: Individual ions confined in EM traps, laser/microwave gates; the highest fidelities and all-to-all connectivity, but slow (~millisecond) gates limit shot throughput.
modalities.strengths: Highest gate fidelity; all-to-all connectivity; long coherence (s-min).
modalities.weaknesses: Slow gates (throughput); laser/optics complexity; scaling ion counts is hard.

best_known.value: 12 logical at ~2e-3 logical error ('reliable quantum computing')
up to ~94 error-protected; 48 from 98 physical at 2:1

modalities.roadmap: Quantinuum Apollo: 100+ qubits; long-term 1,000+ ions below threshold (target). IonQ: photonic interconnect to 1,000+ ions; 800 logical qubits by 2027 (target; no below-threshold demo yet).

modalities.name: Neutral atom
modalities.principle: Neutral atoms in optical tweezer arrays, Rydberg-state entangling gates; reconfigurable connectivity and large arrays, strong recent fault-tolerance progress.
modalities.strengths: Large arrays (1000+); reconfigurable/movable qubits; transversal gates; strong 2025-26 FT results.
modalities.weaknesses: Atom loss; slower cycle times; measurement/reset engineering.

best_known.value: 448-atom: below-threshold surface-code-style QEC + transversal gates + teleportation universality + mid-circuit reuse + constant-entropy deep circuits

modalities.roadmap: Rapid FT progress; considered a top contender for first hundreds of logical qubits alongside superconducting/ion platforms.

modalities.name: Photonic
modalities.principle: Qubits encoded in light (single photons / squeezed states); room-temperature-ish, network-native, measurement-based; PsiQuantum bets on fusion-based FT at fab scale.
modalities.strengths: Coherence-immune (photons don't decohere like matter); networking/interconnect native; silicon-photonics fab.
modalities.weaknesses: Probabilistic gates / photon loss; huge resource-state overhead; detectors need cryo.

best_known.value: fusion-based fault-tolerant photonic; utility-scale system build-outs announced (Brisbane AU, Chicago US)
Borealis quantum-advantage sampling; Aurora networked-modules demo

modalities.roadmap: Long-horizon bet; if the photonic FT approach pays off it scales via manufacturing rather than qubit-by-qubit.

modalities.name: Silicon spin qubit
modalities.principle: Electron/nuclear spins in silicon quantum dots; CMOS-compatible, tiny footprint, high fidelity but early on counts.
modalities.strengths: CMOS/foundry-compatible; smallest qubits; high fidelity; potential for dense integration.
modalities.weaknesses: Very early on qubit counts; uniformity/crosstalk; control wiring.

best_known.value: Tunnel Falls spin-qubit chip on 300mm CMOS line

modalities.roadmap: Betting on foundry manufacturability to scale once per-dot control is solved.

modalities.name: Topological
modalities.principle: Information stored non-locally in anyons/Majorana modes; intrinsically error-protected IF the physics holds - long-contested experimentally.
modalities.strengths: Would be hardware-level error protection (fewer physical qubits per logical).
modalities.weaknesses: Existence/measurement of the underlying quasiparticles remains scientifically contested; least mature.

best_known.value: claimed topological-qubit device; underlying Majorana evidence disputed in the literature

modalities.roadmap: Highest-risk / highest-reward; not yet a demonstrated computing platform.

error_correction.intro: Error correction is the gate to usefulness: physical qubits are far too noisy, so many are combined into fewer, more reliable LOGICAL qubits. Exponential error suppression only kicks in BELOW a physical-error threshold (~1% for surface/qLDPC). 2024-26 crossed that line experimentally; the frontier is now overhead (qLDPC), leakage, universality (magic states / transversal gates), and real-time decoding.

concepts.def: The physical error rate below which adding qubits reduces logical error. ~1% for surface code and high-rate qLDPC (independent depolarizing noise).
Physical qubits per logical qubit. Surface code ~121:1 at distance-11 (plus ancillae); qLDPC far lower; bosonic cat codes push to single digits for one error type.
When a logical qubit outlives its best physical qubit - the minimum bar for QEC to help. Crossed by Google Willow (2.4x).
QEC alone protects only Clifford gates; magic-state cultivation or transversal non-Clifford gates are needed for a universal fault-tolerant computer.

codes.name: Surface code
codes.note: Best-understood; hardware-friendly on 2D grids; overhead is the drawback.

codes.name: qLDPC (e.g. bivariate-bicycle, Vine)
codes.status: IBM Kookaburra qLDPC memory targeted 2026; new planar-grid constructions (Vine, heavy-hex) 2026
codes.note: The overhead-reduction path; the basis of IBM's fault-tolerant roadmap.

codes.name: Cat / bosonic codes
codes.threshold: bit-flip -> ~0 via hardware; phase-flip via outer code
codes.overhead: single digits per logical (one error type)
codes.note: Biases noise so only one error type needs active correction.

codes.name: Color / concatenated / newer nonstabilizer
codes.status: research; some ultrahigh-threshold nonlinear codes proposed 2025-26

milestones.claim: Below-threshold surface code on Willow (distance-7, Lambda=2.14, 2.4x break-even)
Neutral-atom FT ingredients in one 448-atom processor (below-threshold + transversal + teleportation + reuse)
All-microwave leakage suppression below threshold on distance-7 surface code (72x leakage reduction @40 cycles)
Magic-state cultivation on a superconducting processor
12 logical qubits below physical error rate

pqc.intro: Post-quantum cryptography replaces RSA/ECC (breakable by Shor's algorithm) with math believed hard for quantum computers. NIST finalized the first standards in 2024; migration is now a compliance program, not just research. Diversify families - one broken family (SIKE, 2022) shouldn't sink the whole stack.

subareas.note: The workhorses: good sizes/speed. KEM for key exchange, DSA for signatures. Basis of most migration.
Most conservative security (rests only on hash functions); larger/slower. Stateful variants (XMSS/LMS) power firmware signing and QRL's ledger.

subareas.status: McEliece added to ISO asymmetric-ciphers standard (Jun 2026); HQC selected by NIST as the non-lattice backup KEM (Mar 2025, IR 8545) - NIST did NOT standardize Classic McEliece
subareas.note: Decades-old, very conservative; huge public keys (McEliece). ~47 years unbroken for real parameters. 2025-26 saw notable cryptanalysis that is often MISREAD as a break: a quasipolynomial DISTINGUISHER (Ghoshal/Ishai/Jain/Sun, eprint 2026/1630 'PIR Meets McEliece') decides McEliece-vs-random codes (a property never claimed secret) but is impractical to run (smallest case ~2^27-dim system); the Randriambololona syzygy distinguisher (Eurocrypt 2025 best paper, heuristic-dependent); a higher-order-vanishing KEY-RECOVERY (Hemmert, eprint 2026/1339) that improves prior attacks but stays FAR above target security (~2^114-2^124 distinguish vs 2^151-2^287 ISD); and an algebraic SIDE-CHANNEL attack on decapsulation (Springer 2026, implementation leak). Bottom line: NOT a structural break for real parameter sets - distinguisher/theory, unlike SIKE which genuinely fell. NIST did note mceliece460896 dipped below its Category-3 claim (still >= Cat 2).
Cautionary tale: an entire NIST finalist fell to a classical attack - why diversification matters.

subareas.status: symmetric already quantum-resistant with larger keys (Grover -> double key size)
subareas.note: AES-256/SHA-384 need no replacement (only larger sizes); hybrids run classical+PQC together during migration.

compliance.intro: PQC migration is increasingly mandated, with divergent regional timelines, allowed algorithm sets, and restrictions. 'Harvest-now, decrypt-later' makes the deadline effectively already here for long-lived secrets.

regions.mandate: PQC required for National Security Systems; software/firmware signing PQC-ready ~2025, broad adoption phased to 2030-2033
regions.note: ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, LMS/XMSS for firmware, AES-256, SHA-384/512.

regions.mandate: NSM-10 + OMB M-23-02 inventory of cryptographic systems; migrate per NIST standards; CISA/NSA/NIST joint guidance
regions.note: Agencies inventory and prioritize; no single hard cutover date.

regions.mandate: Coordinated PQC transition roadmap (2026); BSI recommends hybrid; ANSSI phased guidance to hybrid then PQC-only
regions.note: Europe leans HYBRID (classical+PQC) during transition; national agencies set specifics.

regions.mandate: Migration timeline to ~2035 with milestones (discovery by 2028, high-priority migration by 2031)

regions.authority: various (e.g. China OSCCA/SM algorithms; export controls)
regions.mandate: Some states mandate national algorithm suites; export-control and sovereignty concerns shape which PQC is 'allowed' where
regions.note: PQC choice is also geopolitical (national suites, procurement rules).

threat.crqc: A cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (CRQC) runs Shor's algorithm at scale to recover RSA/ECC private keys from public keys. Breaking RSA-2048 is broadly estimated to need MILLIONS of physical qubits running deep fault-tolerant circuits.
threat.estimates: Practical quantum advantage on useful (non-crypto) problems: ~2027-2030 (chemistry/optimization). CRQC for RSA-2048: broad estimates 2033-2040+ - wide uncertainty, not a committed date.
threat.harvest_now: Adversaries can capture encrypted data / exposed on-chain public keys today and decrypt once a CRQC exists ('harvest-now, decrypt-later') - which is why long-lived secrets and reused-address chains must migrate BEFORE the machine arrives.
threat.classical_bridge: ECDSA is already fragile CLASSICALLY (weak-nonce key leakage - see the ECDSA.fail tracker); the quantum break is a second, later reason to migrate the signature layer. Same destination, two clocks.
